funder_reqs.funder_name: Florida Department of State, Division of Arts and Culture
eligibility: Applicant organization must be either a public entity or a Florida non-profit, tax-exempt corporation as of the application deadline
All organizations must have at least one year of completed arts and cultural programming and must be able to provide their last completed fiscal year's operating budget
Applicant must have registered with the Division of Corporations and their status must be active
Applicant must be registered as a vendor with the Department of Financial Services and provide a copy of their Florida Substitute W-9 form
Applicant must provide their UEI number at the time of application
Applicant must provide a copy of their most recently completed Federal 990 form

project_narrative.content:
Cinema Verde, the Gainesville Environmental Film and Arts Festival, proposes a Specific Cultural Project to expand its 2026 Annual Environmental Film Festival programming with enhanced community engagement activities, educational workshops, and filmmaker-led discussions that deepen public understanding of environmental issues through the arts.

Founded in 2010, Cinema Verde has hosted 16 annual environmental film festivals, supporting over 200 filmmakers from more than 50 countries. The organization's mission is to provide environmental education to the public through film, arts, workshops, events, tours, and other forums, striving to increase awareness of environmental practices that enhance public health and improve quality of life in urban, suburban, and rural settings. This project directly serves that mission by expanding the festival's educational reach and cultural offerings.

The proposed project centers on a multi-venue festival experience across Gainesville's established cultural venues, including Cypress and Grove Brewing Company, Heartwood Soundstage, the Hippodrome State Theatre, the Historic Depot Station, and the Paramount Plaza Hotel. Each venue will host curated film screenings paired with facilitated discussions led by attending filmmakers, creating direct engagement between audiences and the artists whose work addresses pressing environmental challenges. Building on the 2024 festival, which featured over 75 films, and the 2025 festival, which presented 33 carefully selected films, the proposed project will curate a program that balances breadth of global environmental perspectives with depth of community engagement at each screening.

Quality of Offerings

Cinema Verde's programming quality is rooted in its curatorial process, which draws from an international pool of independent environmental filmmakers. Over 16 festivals, the organization has built relationships with filmmakers from more than 50 countries, resulting in programming that spans documentary, narrative, and experimental approaches to environmental storytelling. The festival's founding director, Trish Riley, is a national award-winning investigative and environmental journalist and author whose published works include The Complete Idiot's Guide to Green Living and The Complete Idiot's Guide to Greening Your Business, both published by Penguin. Her expertise in environmental communication directly informs the festival's curatorial standards and its emphasis on films that combine artistic merit with substantive environmental content.

The proposed project will enhance quality by adding structured post-screening discussions where filmmakers share their creative processes and the environmental research behind their work. These discussions transform passive viewing into active learning experiences, elevating the artistic and educational value of each screening. Additionally, the project includes partnerships with established community organizations including Keep Alachua County Beautiful and We Are Neutral, ensuring that environmental themes explored in the films connect to actionable local initiatives.

Reach and Impact

Cinema Verde's reach extends well beyond Gainesville's local community. The festival has received international media coverage from outlets including Authority Magazine, Yahoo Finance, Causeartist, The Ecologist, and World Future TV, as well as international press from outlets in Germany including OXMOX Hamburg and Freudenstoff. This media presence amplifies the impact of each festival beyond its in-person attendees.

The proposed project will expand reach through several strategies. First, educational workshops at community venues will engage audiences who may not typically attend film screenings, broadening the demographic reach of the festival's programming. These workshops will be designed to connect film content to practical environmental action, building on Cinema Verde's history of community-facing programming such as Earth Day celebrations, community cleanups including the Ashley Creek cleanup, and local film screenings at venues like Cypress and Grove Brewing Company. Second, the project will leverage Cinema Verde's existing environmental film streaming platform at cinemaverde.org and its Roku channel, which provides free year-round access to curated environmental films from independent filmmakers worldwide, to extend the impact of festival programming well beyond the event dates and make content accessible to audiences who cannot attend in person. Third, additional community events will provide hands-on environmental engagement opportunities that complement the festival's film programming and create multiple points of entry for community members to engage with environmental content throughout the project period.

The organization's partnership with the University of Florida through the UNLITTER UF initiative demonstrates its commitment to engaging younger audiences and building environmental awareness among college students. The Sustainable Business Spotlight program further extends reach by connecting environmental film content to local business practices, engaging the business community in sustainability conversations.

Track Record

Cinema Verde's 16-year track record demonstrates consistent organizational capacity and fiscal responsibility. The organization operates as a 501(c)(3) public charity and Florida nonprofit corporation with a transparent financial structure. In its most recently completed fiscal year, Cinema Verde reported total revenue of $143,935, with program services generating $104,330 and contributions accounting for $39,605. Total expenses were $151,470, and the organization maintains net assets of $174,573, demonstrating a stable financial foundation.

The organization operates with a small, dedicated team of under 10 staff members, with key personnel including Founding Director Trish Riley, Technical Director and Webmaster Thomas Berning, and Writer and Contributor Christine Heinrichs. The board of directors includes Thomas Berning and Rachel Rector. All key staff and board members report zero compensation, reflecting the organization's commitment to directing resources toward programming rather than administrative overhead. Cinema Verde relies heavily on interns and volunteers representing an array of nationalities, which both reduces operational costs and enriches the festival's international character.

Cinema Verde has previously received one grant totaling $25,000, demonstrating the organization's ability to secure and manage grant funding responsibly. This prior grant experience, combined with 16 years of continuous festival production, reflects an organization that has built sustainable operations despite its small size. The consistent growth in programming scope, from early festivals to the 2024 festival featuring over 75 films from around the world, demonstrates an upward trajectory in both programming ambition and organizational capacity. The organization is a registered Florida nonprofit corporation, holds solicitation license CH33749, and maintains its tax-exempt status under EIN 27-3021913. Cinema Verde is a member of Pledge 1%, further reflecting its commitment to community-oriented operations and responsible organizational stewardship.

History and Heritage Promotion

The proposed project promotes Florida's cultural heritage by showcasing the state's role in environmental arts and education. Over 16 years, Cinema Verde has established Gainesville as a recognized destination for international environmental filmmaking, contributing to the city's cultural identity and supporting Florida's creative economy. The festival has screened films from over 50 countries across its history, bringing global environmental perspectives to Florida audiences while highlighting the state's own environmental landscape and challenges. The festival's use of historic and culturally significant venues, including the Hippodrome State Theatre and the Historic Depot Station, roots the programming in Florida's arts heritage while addressing contemporary environmental concerns. Community events such as Earth Day celebrations and sustainability showcases connect environmental awareness to local traditions and ways of life, reinforcing the connection between Florida's natural environment and its cultural character. The Sustainable Business Spotlight program further ties the festival to Florida's economic heritage by recognizing local businesses committed to sustainable practices.

The proposed project budget requests funding to support venue rentals, filmmaker travel and accommodations, marketing and outreach for expanded programming, materials for educational workshops, and coordination of community engagement events. All proposed activities will be completed within the grant period and are designed to be open, accessible, and appropriate for all members of the public. The project's multi-venue approach ensures geographic accessibility across Gainesville, and all venues will comply with accessibility requirements to ensure programming is inclusive of individuals with disabilities.

Cinema Verde's track record of successful festival production, its established venue partnerships, its international network of filmmakers, and its commitment to environmental education through the arts position the organization to deliver a high-quality, impactful project that serves the Division's mission to advance, support, and promote arts and culture to strengthen the economy and quality of life for all Floridians.
